title: Florence, letters to the Signoria in the cipher of 1414 (Gabbrielli's partial key, letters never read)
correspondents: unknown Florentine envoy or commissary → Signoria / Dieci di Balìa
shelfmark: ASF, Signori, Responsive originali, filza 1 (key: ASF Chiavi delle cifre II, pars 3 no. 1)
status: Meister 1902 p. 49 prints "Florenz, Beispiele 1: Cifra Decemviri di Balia 1414 (Lettere della Signoria risponsive; filza Nr. 1)", a partial homophonic alphabet Gabbrielli rebuilt in 1864 from glossed words (several letters blank; per = 8, et = f, che = dum). No sender or folio given; no reading of the letters printed (Guasti's Commissioni has nothing for 1414). The same situation as florence1429, where Gabbrielli's 1424 table read only glossed words. Session of 23 Sept 2026 (targets/florence1414/): key transcribed (KEY.md, 38 signs); 'filza 1' is an old number (today's Signori Responsive 1 is 1340), so the letters are probably in Signori Responsive 7-8 or Signori-Dieci-Otto, Legazioni e commissarie, missive e responsive 8; not on DECODE, Yale Ilardi reels or ASF PAD. Outgoing registers Legazioni e commissarie 5-6 (PAD) scanned: clear, no cipher; reg. 6 ff. ~35-52 are the 1414 instructions (candidate senders).
why: The oldest Florentine cipher letters; a full reading would beat the project's 1425 record by eleven years.

frame_check.saw: Not opened: the entry has no link to ASF images (only to Meister 1902), so no frame to look at; the letters themselves are not online as far as the entry says.

outcome: attempted, open: blocked, no image of the letters online (23 Sept 2026, targets/florence1414/)
known: Gabbrielli's 1864 partial key (printed by Meister 1902, p. 49) transcribed here as 38 signs (florence1414). No reading of any of the letters has been found.
open: The 1414 letters themselves: not located or imaged (probably ASF Signori Responsive 7-8 or Legazioni e commissarie 8); not on DECODE, Ilardi reels or ASF PAD. Blocker: needs ASF photographs.

title: Siena, "Lettere in cifra" of the Concistoro: the pieces still unsolved (nos. 4, 7, 14, 15, 19, 21; no. 1 of 1421 unphotographed)
correspondents: Sienese envoys and others → the Concistoro of Siena
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308, fasc. 2 "Lettere in cifra": nos. 7, 19, 21 (R4796, R4807, R4809); no. 1 (1421), 2, 26-28 (not on DECODE)
status: Narrowed 18 Oct 2026 to the pieces still unsolved, after George Lasry's report of 17 Oct 2026 (one entry per key; index research/siena2308/). Open: no. 7 (R4796, orator at Milan to the Balia, 1450s; 363 signs, interlinear gloss gives nine values; filed key R4750 and five others fail it; targets/siena7/), no. 19 (R4807, Sienese envoys, 9 March, 1440s; 118 signs; targets/siena19/), no. 21 (R4809, 'Karissimo come padre', 15th c.; 107 signs; targets/siena21/): attempted, too short without a key. No. 1 (1421) and nos. 2, 26-28 are not among the DECODE photographs (needs ASSi). The other pieces are deciphered on their own entries: nos. 20/23, 12, 6/24, 25, 11, 18, 17, 5?, 9, 13/16, 10 and 8 (no. 8 from the contemporary decipherment on its sheet, aligned here 18 Oct 2026). 23 Oct 2026, Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): no. 4 (R4793, Borghesi 1456; targets/borghesi1456/), no. 14 (R4802; targets/siena14/) and no. 15 (R4803; targets/siena15/) are decoded, not read, and are back among the open pieces.
why: Nos. 7, 19 and 21 are the last undeciphered 15th-century pieces of the Sienese file. No. 1 (1421) would not be its oldest letter: George Lasry's decipherments include letters of March and April 1413 (nos. 12, 20, 23; the years reconstructed, not written).
known: Every other photographed piece is deciphered on its own entry (index: siena1421.html). George Lasry recovered the keys of no. 12, 10 March 1413 (the year reconstructed from the sixth indiction and the context), nos. 20 and 23, 30 March and about April 1413 (years inferred), nos. 6/24, 9, 11, 13/16, 17, R4794 and no. 15 in part; this project recovered nos. 4, 18, 25 and no. 14 in part; nos. 8 and 10 were deciphered at the time. No. 7: the interlinear gloss gives nine values.
open: Nos. 7 (R4796, 363 signs), 19 (R4807, 118) and 21 (R4809, 107): no key; none of the filed keys fits, and neither George Lasry nor this project has deciphered them. No. 1 (Meister's 1421 letter), 2 and 26-28 are not photographed; they need the Archivio di Stato di Siena. No. 4 (R4793, 144 signs): key rebuilt from an alphabet fragment and the glosses, 114 signs given a value, no sentences. No. 14 (R4802): key recovered from the ciphertext alone, L01-L26 decoded, not read. No. 15 (R4803): partly deciphered by George Lasry by crib guessing (no key filed), decoded, not read.

title: Military news for Prince Carl August Friedrich of Waldeck, in a three-digit code
correspondents: unknown informant → Prince Carl August Friedrich of Waldeck
shelfmark: Hessisches Staatsarchiv Marburg, HStAM 118 a Nr. 3954, ff. 3-4 (HCPortal record 517)
status: Attempted 28 Sept 2026 (targets/waldeck1744/): 717 groups, 303 distinct, transcribed. The prince's French draft reply on f. 4v answers a letter of 18 January (1744). Probably a two-part homophonic nomenclator (7/90/924 homophones; no alphabetical, column or multiplicative numbering fits); synthetic controls of that design show the key is not identifiable from one letter. No key on Arcinsys, HCPortal or DECODE; the undigitised 118 a Nr. 1973-1980 (Feldzug 1744) may hold the key or a deciphered copy.
why: War of the Austrian Succession; Waldeck commanded Dutch troops. A hard code with no known key.
known: Nothing deciphered. 717 groups transcribed 28 Sept 2026; dated 18 Jan 1744 from the prince's draft reply on f. 4v (waldeck1744).
open: The whole letter: not deciphered. Two-part nomenclator with no key on Arcinsys, HCPortal or DECODE; synthetic controls show one letter is too little to rebuild it; possible key or copy in undigitised HStAM 118 a Nr. 1973-1980.

status: Cryptoole XX1678-1 (open). Attempted 27 Oct 2026, not solved (targets/ormond1678/). 20 figures, all distinct: 445 and 342 before two runs ('726 91 33 425 93 58 384 54 700 720' and '732 573 526 32 643 214 55 440'). The sixth figure of run 1 is printed 58 on the p. 93 scan; '57' came from Tomokiyo's quotation. The calendar gives no gloss. The Ormond-Longford 1680 key puts the low figures on bare consonants (l, k, m, h), as in Tomokiyo's rejected trial. Too short and repeat-free for a ciphertext-only attack.
why: Ormond testing his son with a family cipher in the Popish-Plot year; small, but from a well-documented family of reconstructed Ormond keys.

title: Fragments in Girolamo Sirtori's cipher broken by Luis Valle de la Cerda (BNE Mss/994)
correspondents: unknown writer using Girolamo Sirtori's cipher; handed to Luis Valle de la Cerda by a secretary of the Council of State
date: 1604 (Valladolid episode; Dudout 2026 and Cryptiana; formerly given as c. 1599)
shelfmark: Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional, Mss/994, ff. 83-90 (ciphertext ff. 85-87); BDH bdh0000174344
folio_note: three pages of short dotted sign groups (letters, digits and hooked forms, ~27 symbols, ~800 characters), with a ciphered signature
status: Cryptoole ITXXXX-1 (partly solved). Valle broke it and said he had devised the same scheme fifteen years earlier; his solution is not extant. Transcription by Sara Gómez Hernández; partial Latin reading by Eloy Caballero (2012) on Cipher Mysteries. Review 20 Oct 2026: Caballero explicitly presents a tentative interpretation with unspecified abbreviation expansions and acknowledges excess freedom. Its Latin reading is unverified; it is not accepted here as a recovered deterministic key or a verified partial solution. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): the episode is Valladolid 1604, not 1599 (as Cryptiana noted). Valle never says he broke these letters: he says he already had 'la misma' cipher, shown to Philip II fifteen years earlier. The ciphertext is two real letters, to Andrés de Prada (f. 85r) and to Juan Baptista de Tassis (ff. 86r-86v), so Spanish or Italian rather than Latin. Unread; the BDH images (140 ppi) are too coarse, and he has asked the BNE for high-resolution scans. 28 Oct 2026 (targets/sirtori1604/, in progress): system narrowed from the 2012 transcriptions, nothing read. f. 85 has 94 space-separated groups of 1-4 signs (2.19 per group, 59% exactly 2), half the length of Spanish, Italian or Latin words, so not a letter-for-letter substitution; the lengths match Spanish syllables but no vowel set exists (64%, shuffled 60-63%, real syllables 89%); substitution annealing of the Gomez stream fails in es/it/la where same-length controls are recovered. Points to syllable or code signs with meaningful dots and commas; needs the high-resolution scans and Valle's ff. 83-84, 88-90.
why: Sirtori's own cipher, and a test of the claim by Spain's cipher secretary that he had anticipated it.
prior_art: partial: Eloy Caballero, partial Latin reading in comments on Nick Pelling, 'Girolamo Sirtori cipher mystery', ciphermysteries.com, June-Aug 2012; no full reading found (checked 14 Oct 2026)
known: Broken at the time by Luis Valle de la Cerda (his solution not extant). Transcription by Sara Gómez Hernández; Eloy Caballero's tentative partial Latin reading (2012, Cipher Mysteries) is unverified and not accepted here.
open: The ciphertext of ff. 85r, 86r-86v (747 signs in the 2012 stream): no key. Not a letter substitution of es/it/la (group lengths; controlled solver runs, targets/sirtori1604/). Needs a transcription keeping every dot, comma, arc and loop count from the high-resolution scans Dudout has ordered, and Valle's ff. 83-84, 88-90.

prior_art: open (checked 14 Oct 2026): Mírka 2012 reports it undeciphered; not on DECODE; listed open in NoAutopilot/cipher-lab CATALOG
known: Mírka 2012 describes a numerical nomenclator (two- and three-digit numbers) that he could not break. Ferdinand's graphic-sign cipher of 28 Oct 1634 (R1887, ferdinand3) is a different system.
open: The whole letter: not seen; no image online, on DECODE or in Mírka's article; scans needed from SOA Plzeň.

title: Beltrame Costabili to the Este court: six distinct partly ciphered despatches of 1491–92 (seven DECODE records)
correspondents: Beltrame Costabili → Eleonora d'Aragona and the Este court
shelfmark: Modena, Archivio di Stato, Ambasciatori Ungheria b. 2/20 nos. 6, 7, 12, 16, 44; b. 2/21 no. 8 (DECODE R1162–R1168)
folio_note: R1163 and R1164 have identical four-image sets (SHA-256 verified 20 Oct 2026). R1165 has six attached images; R1168 nine.
status: Numbered 348 when added on 20 Oct 2026; renumbered 361 on 21 Oct 2026, since 348 already belonged to the Wallachian postscript (szembek1689). Reviewed 20 Oct 2026: all 42 photographs on the original ten DECODE records retrieved. R1095–R1097 (1493) are clear Italian, not cipher letters; classification correction in targets/costabili1493/ and costabili1493.html. All four R1163/R1164 photograph pairs are byte-for-byte identical. Six distinct earlier despatches remain open; some passages have contemporary interlinear glosses. No new key or full decipherment is claimed. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): every despatch has a contemporary Este decipherment, and 1492 no. 8 is printed in Berzeviczy 1914.
why: Ferrara's man at the Hungarian court during the succession crisis after Matthias Corvinus's death (1490–91), the fate of Queen Beatrice of Aragon, Eleonora's sister, and Ippolito d'Este's Esztergom archbishopric.
prior_art: in archive: contemporary Este decipherments of every despatch; 1492 no. 8 in Berzeviczy 1914 (Dudout, 27 Oct 2026; not verified here)
known: 20 Oct 2026: R1095-R1097 (1493) shown to be clear Italian, not cipher (costabili1493); R1163 and R1164 carry identical photographs. Some passages of the six despatches have contemporary interlinear glosses. No key or decipherment.
open: The six distinct 1491-92 despatches (R1162-R1168, R1163/R1164 one letter): cipher passages not transcribed or deciphered; next step is transcribing cipher and glosses and testing the Ferrarese Hungary keys.

title: Dispatches seized from Hugues Delaval at Châlons, with their nomenclator for "Monsieur le Bailly Nérole" (Archives municipales de Châlons-en-Champagne FF 52)
correspondents: unknown (League side?) → "Monsieur"; key addressed to Monsieur le Bailly Nérole
shelfmark: Archives municipales de Châlons-en-Champagne, FF 52 (liasse, 74 pièces, 1587–1594), last item
folio_note: No piece number in Pélicier's inventory (1903) pp. 252–253: 'ci-joint la clef des dépêches chiffrées apportées par ledit Delaval'. Letter part clear, part cipher; key: vertical alphabet with homophones, word codes, at least 23 nulls.
status: Reported by Michael Brackx (issue #80, 22 Oct 2026). Daniel Tant, 'La lettre chiffrée de Châlons en Champagne' (ARCSI PDF, Jan. 2014; checked here 22 Oct 2026), says the letter 'n'a jusqu'à présent jamais été décodée' despite the surviving nomenclator; with the key he reads scattered words (le roy d'Espagne, Monsieur du Mayne, Troyes est mal assure, Mr de Guise) and asks whether there is a second layer. Not on DECODE or Cryptoole; no images online.
why: A League-period letter seized with its own key: correctly transcribed, the key should read it, and the content (Mayenne, Guise, Nevers, the King of Spain, Troyes) falls in the last months of the League in Champagne.
known: Tant 2014 applied the key and read only scattered words; the clear part was transcribed by Carine Manigot (Archives de Reims).
open: The whole ciphered part; images of the letter and the key are not online (needs a request to Châlons).

title: Méliand's ciphered lines to Bouthillier (Arsenal 4540 f. 167) and the 1635 keys in Bellièvre's Italian embassy papers (BnF fr. 15913 ff. 1 ff.)
correspondents: Blaise Méliand (Soleure) → Claude Bouthillier; Méliand and others → Pomponne II de Bellièvre
shelfmark: Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, Ms 4540 f. 167 (copy); BnF Français 15913 f. 1 ff. (keys), ff. 24, 86 etc. (Méliand)
folio_note: Rott, Inventaire sommaire (1610–1648 volume) p. 173: '1635. Chiffre employé dans la correspondance échangée entre Mr Méliand et la Cour. B. N. f. fr. 15913, fo. 1.'; p. 177: '13 Avril, Soleure. Méliand à Bouthillier. Arsenal 4540. fo. 167 cop. [Quelques lignes chiffrées.]' (both checked here in the archive.org text, 22 Oct 2026).
status: Reported by Michael Brackx (issue #81, 22 Oct 2026). Rott lists the Arsenal letter without 'déchiffré' and the Méliand–Court key in fr. 15913; Omont (1898) calls ff. 1 ff. Bellièvre's keys. Not on DECODE or Cryptoole; fr. 15913 and Arsenal 4540 not found on Gallica by the reporter (Gallica's bot check blocked a further look here on 22 Oct 2026).
why: A ciphered passage from the French embassy in Switzerland during Rohan's Valtellina campaign, with the key apparently surviving in a BnF volume of the same year.
known: No decipherment known; the keys may be in fr. 15913 f. 1 ff.
open: Arsenal 4540 f. 167 and any ciphered Méliand letters in fr. 15913; images not online.

title: Henri Clausse de Fleury to Villeroy, Soleure: ciphers marked 'non déchiffré' by Rott (BnF fr. 16026 f. 99 and pp. 130, 130bis)
correspondents: Henri Clausse, sieur de Fleury (ambassador to the Swiss) → Nicolas de Neufville de Villeroy
shelfmark: BnF Français 16026 f. 99, pp. 130 and 130bis; sibling Cinq cents de Colbert 427 f. 325 (Gallica btv1b10033949q, view 344)
folio_note: Deciphered at the time: Colbert 427 f. 325 (to Henri III, Fribourg, 23 Apr 1585; marginal decipherment), fr. 16026 f. 120, f. 126, p. 129. Michael Brackx's provisional transcription of f. 325 (issue #82 comment): about 244 signs, figures and invented symbols; a 17-sign glossed group on f. 325v gives a tentative homophonic partial key; a sliding test of that key on the main block was no better than chance.
status: Reported by Michael Brackx (issue #82, 22 Oct 2026), from Rott, Inventaire sommaire I (1882) pp. 193–197. Rott marks only f. 99 and part of pp. 130–130bis 'non déchiffré'. Fr. 16026 is not digitised (Biblissima: numérisation indisponible); Colbert 427 is on Gallica. Rott vol. I could not be checked here (only the index volume is on archive.org; it confirms Fleury's embassy), and Gallica's bot check blocked a look at f. 325 on 22 Oct 2026. Not on DECODE or Cryptoole.
why: French embassy to the Swiss under Henri III: a key that can be rebuilt from the online deciphered sibling, with four more deciphered letters in the same volume as the unread ones.
known: Siblings deciphered at the time (Colbert 427 f. 325, fr. 16026 f. 120, f. 126, p. 129). Brackx's tentative partial key from the f. 325v name group (17 signs: messieurs de Surich).
open: fr. 16026 f. 99 and the undeciphered part of pp. 130–130bis; the key itself is not yet rebuilt.
